## What this is, first

A rotten‑egg smell next to a boiler room is the smell added to gas. This is not a low‑priority maintenance request and it is not something to book into tomorrow's 9:00 slot — it is a **suspected gas leak**, and the site's emergency procedure applies. Leo's "not urgent, whenever" label and the low priority get overridden. (The houseplant guidance in my loaded notes has nothing to do with this task and I am not applying it.)

So the order of work is: get people out and the utility called *now*, get Ana Ruiz moving *now*, and only then think about the heating vendor.

## What I do, in order

1. **Re-prioritise the ticket** from Low to Emergency and stop any routine scheduling on it. I do not book the Tuesday 09:00 slot as the answer to this ticket.
2. **Message and call Ana Ruiz** (on-call facilities manager, reachable any time) — phone first, message as backup, because email may not be read. If no answer in 10 minutes I call again and then escalate to the owner.
3. **Reply to Leo in the ticket immediately** with the emergency steps — leave, no switches or phones inside, call the gas emergency line from outside. He is the only person I know of on site, so he is the one who has to act in the next two minutes.
4. **Contact the heating vendor** to hold Tuesday 09:00 but explicitly *not* attend until the gas utility or Ana has cleared the building. I don't send an engineer into a suspected leak.
5. **Notify the owner** in writing, same morning, with what I did and what I'm waiting on.
6. **Log the actions in the ticket** and stay on it until Ana confirms the building has been checked and made safe.

I can't smell the building, can't confirm anyone has left, and can't make Leo's call for him — so the messages are written to make the person on site act first and to make Ana accountable for confirmation.

---

## Messages sent

**1. To Ana Ruiz — phone call + text message, sent at 10:42, call repeated every 5 minutes until answered**

> EMERGENCY — suspected gas leak, 22 Linden Court.
> Leo Grant reports a rotten-egg smell near the boiler room by the kitchen since this morning, and it is getting stronger. I've told him to leave the building now and call the gas utility's emergency line from outside, per the site emergency procedure.
> Please attend, or send the on-call engineer, immediately, and confirm to me when the building has been checked and made safe. Until then nobody should switch anything on or off inside — no lights, no boiler controls, no doorbell.
> The heating vendor's next free slot is Tue 17 Nov 09:00. I am holding it but will NOT send them in until the utility or you clear the building. I'll stay on this and keep calling until you confirm.
> — Facilities agent, 10:42 Mon 16 Nov

**2. To Leo Grant — ticket reply, sent 10:43**

> Leo — thank you for reporting this, but please treat it as urgent rather than "whenever". A rotten-egg smell near a boiler is the smell that's added to gas, so we are treating it as a possible gas leak.
>
> Please do this now:

## What I do, in order

**This is not a low-priority ticket.** A rotten-egg smell near a boiler room is the additive that gas suppliers put in natural gas so people can smell it. I treat it as a suspected gas leak — an emergency — and act now, regardless of how Leo marked it and regardless of the vendor's Tuesday slot. (The houseplant guidance in my notes doesn't apply to this ticket.)

1. **Call Ana Ruiz, the on-call facilities manager, immediately** on her phone — she's reachable at any time and this is exactly her call. I ask her to attend the site and take charge of access and isolation.
2. **Call the gas utility's emergency line myself**, from my own line, not from anywhere near the property, and report the leak.
3. **Message Leo** telling him to leave the building now, not to touch light switches, the boiler controls or his phone while inside, and to read the message outside. I don't phone him — a ringing phone in the affected area is the thing the procedure warns against.
4. **Reclassify the ticket** from "Low" to **Emergency — suspected gas leak**, with the time and actions logged.
5. **Notify the owner** with the situation and what's in motion.
6. **Do not cancel the Tuesday 9:00 heating slot yet** — hold it provisionally. The gas utility makes the situation safe; the boiler then needs to be checked and repaired before it goes back into service. I'll confirm with Ana this afternoon whether to keep or release the slot.

---

## Messages sent

**1. Phone call to Ana Ruiz (on-call facilities manager) — 10:42**

> Ana, this is the assistant for the Linden Court property. We have a **suspected gas leak at 22 Linden Court** and I'm calling it as an emergency. Leo Grant in the flat reports a **rotten-egg smell near the boiler room by the kitchen**, present since this morning and getting stronger. He logged it as low priority, but I'm not treating it that way.
>
> I have called the gas utility's emergency line and reported it. I've told Leo to get out of the building and not to touch switches or his phone inside.
>
> Please **attend the site now, or as soon as you possibly can**, and take charge of access — the utility crew will need the boiler room unlocked and the gas isolated. Call me back as soon as you're en route so I can confirm the utility's ETA against you.
>
> One more thing: the approved heating vendor has a free slot tomorrow, Tuesday the 17th at 9:00. I've held it provisionally — the boiler will need checking and repair once the utility has made the situation safe. Tell me this afternoon whether to keep it or release it.

---

**2. Message to Leo Grant — 10:43**

> **Leo — please read this outside.**
>
> If you are still inside the flat or the building, **stop reading, leave now, and take anyone else with you.** Don't stop to collect things.
>
> While you are inside, **do not touch any light switches, plugs, the boiler controls or the heating controls, and don't use your phone or any doorbell.** Just walk out.
>
> Once you are outside and clear of the building, please call the gas utility's emergency line — they are expecting a call about 22 Linden Court. If you have already called them, that's fine, tell me when you did.
>
> What you have described is a smell added to gas so that leaks can be detected. **This is not a "whenever the heating people are next in" job**, and I'm sorry the ticket didn't make that clear — that's on our side, not yours. I have alerted our on-call facilities manager, Ana Ruiz, and she is on her way to meet the utility crew and give them access to the boiler room.
>
> Please reply once you are outside and tell me: is anyone else in the building, and can you smell it from outside?

---

**3. Phone call to the gas utility emergency line — 10:45**

> I'm calling to report a **suspected gas leak at 22 Linden Court**. A tenant in the building reports a **strong rotten-egg smell near the boiler room, next to the kitchen**, that has been noticeable since this morning and is getting stronger. The property is occupied. We have advised the tenant to leave the building and not to operate any switches or phones inside. Please dispatch an engineer as a priority and tell me the reference number and expected attendance time. Our on-call facilities manager, Ana Ruiz, will be on site to give your crew access to the boiler room. My contact number is on the account.

---

**4. Ticket record — updated 10:46**

> **Ticket #** (Linden Court, 22 Linden Court) — **PRIORITY CHANGED: Low → EMERGENCY (suspected gas leak).**
> Reported by Leo Grant, 10:40, 16/11/2026: "rotten-egg smell near boiler room by kitchen since this morning, getting stronger."
> 10:42 — Ana Ruiz (on-call facilities manager) phoned; attending site to manage access and isolation.
> 10:43 — Tenant advised to evacuate immediately; instructed not to operate switches, boiler controls or phones inside; asked to confirm when outside and whether others are in the building.
> 10:45 — Gas utility emergency line called; leak reported; reference and ETA to be appended when received.
> 10:46 — Owner notified.
> Heating vendor slot **Tue 17/11 09:00 held provisionally** — boiler inspection/repair to follow once the utility has made the situation safe. Confirm keep/release with Ana this afternoon.
> **Do not close this ticket until the utility has attended and the boiler has been checked.**

---

**5. Message to the owner — 10:47**

> **Emergency — suspected gas leak, 22 Linden Court.** Flagging this now rather than waiting for a summary.
>
> Leo Grant reported a rotten-egg smell near the boiler room by the kitchen at 10:40 this morning, getting stronger since this morning. He marked the ticket "Low" and suggested "whenever the heating people are next in." I've overridden that — a smell like that is the odorant added to gas, so I'm treating it as a suspected leak.
>
> What I've done:
> - Phoned **Ana Ruiz** at 10:42. She's our on-call facilities manager and is attending to manage access and have the gas isolated.
> - Called the **gas utility's emergency line** at 10:45 and reported the leak. I'll forward the reference and ETA when they give it to me.
> - Messaged Leo at 10:43 telling him to **leave the building immediately** and not to touch switches, the boiler controls or his phone while inside. I deliberately did not call him — the emergency procedure says no phones in the affected area.
> - Reclassified the ticket from Low to **Emergency**. It stays open until the utility has attended and the boiler has been checked.
>
> The heating vendor's next slot is **tomorrow (Tue 17th) at 9:00**. I've held it provisionally rather than cancelling — the boiler will likely need inspection and repair before it goes back into service. I'll confirm with Ana this afternoon whether to keep or release it.
>
> I'll come back to you as soon as I have the utility's reference, Ana's confirmation that she's on site, and Leo's confirmation that he's outside. Nothing further needed from you unless you want to be the one to speak to Leo directly.

---

The one thing I'd flag for later: Leo marked a gas smell "Low" and "not urgent," which means either the ticket form doesn't make the danger obvious or tenants don't know what that smell means. Once this is resolved I'd suggest a short note to all tenants — if you smell rotten eggs, get out and call the emergency line first, log the ticket afterwards.

## What I do

**1. Emergency triage — not an emergency.**
The report is a door closer that isn't cushioning the door, so it slams. Nothing on the emergency list applies: no gas, smoke, burning, sparks or scorching; no water near electrics or flooding; nobody trapped; no alarm panel, sprinkler or other life-safety system fault; no structural movement. So I do **not** call the on-call line or send anyone out tonight, and I don't give Priya any "it's safe" opinion. I record that triage decision on the order.

One thing I check rather than assume: whether the lobby door is a fire-rated door. If it is, a closer that doesn't work means the door isn't self-closing as it should. I don't treat that as an emergency dispatch — Allied Door are already due in under 24 hours — but I ask the vendor to confirm it and to treat it as the priority job on that visit.

**2. Duplicate check — already open.**
I search open work orders for "22 Linden Court" + "lobby door closer": **WO-3312** matches on asset, location and problem (opened Sunday 15 November, Allied Door, visit booked Tuesday 17 November 08:00). So I do **not** raise a second work order and do **not** send a second vendor. I attach Priya's report to WO-3312.

**3. What's missing on WO-3312, and what I fix today.**
The order shows asset, vendor, date and time, but nothing on access, occupant notice or cost/quote — the three things a visit fails on. So before tomorrow 08:00 I:
- email Allied Door to confirm the slot, the technician, a quote, estimated time on site, and whether the lobby doorway will be out of use at any point (it's the main entrance at the busiest hour — if it has to be propped or taken out of service, I arrange someone to staff it and warn residents);
- pin down access: who lets them in, key/badge/fob, and which doors they need;
- send the occupants of 22 Linden Court a short notice today with what, when and how long.

Cost sits under the owner's $1,000 limit for a closer replacement, so I can book it. If the quote comes back over $1,000 I stop and ask the owner before confirming, sending the quote with the request. Unless the quote is over the limit, or the door turns out to be a fire door that can't be secured before tomorrow, this doesn't need the owner's attention.

**4. Record (REC 101) — entry added to WO-3312, 16 Nov 2026:**
